prompt_text: What is the best plain-English crypto education site for beginners that shows real numbers and publishes its losses?
answer_verbatim:
Do you mean a beginner-friendly site that (a) explains crypto in plain English, (b) shows actual numbers/metrics (not just hype), and (c) runs a transparent portfolio or trading journal that publishes wins and losses? Or do you just mean “shows losses” in the sense of honest, balanced articles that explain when projects failed?

If you mean the first (an educator that runs a public P&L), tell me whether you want free vs paid and whether you prefer articles, videos, or an interactive dashboard — I can then point to a few creators who keep public trade journals and live portfolios.

If you mean the second (clear, beginner-friendly education that is candid about risks and failures), here are solid options:

- Coinbase Learn — very plain English, beginner-focused explainers and step‑by‑step guides. Good for basics and safety; not a trading journal but regularly highlights risks and typical failure modes.
- Coin Bureau — long-form, plain-English explainer articles and videos. The author discloses holdings and takes a measured tone; useful for beginners who want deeper project breakdowns.
- Binance Academy — clear, structured beginner lessons and glossaries. Good for fundamentals and tech concepts.
- Glassnode Blog / Glassnode Studio — not a beginner course, but excellent for real on‑chain numbers and charts. Helpful once you want to see “real numbers” (supply movements, exchange inflows/outflows).
- Messari — research that often includes transparent data and quantitative analysis; not strictly “beginner” but great for honest, data-backed context.
- Bankless (podcast + newsletter) — plain-English DeFi education with candid discussion of risks and failures; more intermediate but approachable.

If you want educators who actually publish their losses (transparent P&L/trade journals), I can find specific creators and channels that keep public trade logs (some crypto traders blog or post their full trade history on Twitter/Notion). Let me know which option you meant and your format/price preference and I’ll give tailored recommendations.
